name: Eliashib
overview: Eliashib was a male Levite known primarily as the father of Jehohanan. His identity as a Levite is confirmed in Nehemiah 12:23, and he is notably mentioned in Ezra 10:6 as the head of the household where the scribe Ezra mourned. This situates Eliashib within the priestly tribe of Levi during the post-exilic period.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliashib means "G-d restores," reflecting a theologically rich meaning tied to God's restorative power. This proper name, as recorded in Ezra 10:6, was not given directly by God but carries significant spiritual connotations consistent with the biblical narrative.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Eliashib as the father of Jehohanan, as inferred from Ezra 10:6. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Eliashib's significance lies in his role as a Levite and the head of the household where Ezra mourned, indicating his household's involvement in the communal repentance and covenant renewal. His position as a Levite connects him to the priestly service and the spiritual restoration of Israel after the exile. Through his family connection to Jehohanan, Eliashib is linked to the community of returned exiles committed to upholding the Law of God.
